subject: Request: IR summary + SOC2/SIG evidence handoff after customer-facing event
messages:
From: Alicia Reyes <alicia.reyes@graysonbank.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: security-team@graysonbank.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:14:00 -0400
Subject: Briefing & request: customer-facing incident — evidence + IR plan

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the quick heads-up this morning about the authentication anomaly that impacted a small subset of our test tenants. Grayson Bank has a compliance window for notifying our internal auditors and external regulators, and they need two things from Redwood by EOD Thursday: a short incident summary for our internal record (timeline, scope, mitigation) and a copy of your incident response plan and SOC2/SIG control mapping relevant to auth/session handling.

Specifically we need:
- High-level incident summary (who/what/when/impact) suitable for our audit team
- Your current IR plan (any redline or version notes are fine)
- SIG/SOC2 mapping for controls tied to authentication, session management, and logging
- A small sample of access logs for the 2027-05-17 02:00–06:00 UTC window (sanitized) so our forensics team can correlate

Can you confirm you can provide these and the expected delivery time? If helpful, loop in the security contact on your side — I've cc'd our security distribution here.

Appreciate it — Alicia

Alicia Reyes
Director, Information Security
Grayson Bank
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Alicia Reyes <alicia.reyes@graysonbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:46:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Briefing & request: customer-facing incident — evidence + IR plan

Alicia — thanks for the clear list. We can provide everything on that list. I'm looping in Marissa (security lead) and Neha (compliance) to coordinate the artifacts and the sanitized log export.

Target: we'll deliver the incident summary and IR plan PDF within 24 hours, and the SIG/SOC2 mapping plus the log sample by EOD Thursday (2027-05-20) to match your audit window. If we hit any blocker for the log sample (PII redaction or retention policy checks) we'll escalate immediately.

Short next steps:
- Marissa: can you confirm the IRP PDF we'll share and produce a sanitized log sample?
- Neha: can you attach the SOC2/SIG control map and confirm any redactions needed for sharing?

Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, Alicia Reyes <alicia.reyes@graysonbank.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 13:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Briefing & request: customer-facing incident — evidence + IR plan

Alicia / Vanessa / Neha —

We have prepared the following and attached them to a secure share: Redwood_IRP_v2.pdf (version notes included), soc2_control_map.csv (filters applied to authentication/session controls), and a sanitized sample of access logs for 2027-05-17 02:00–06:00 UTC. The sanitized log includes session ids hashed and IPs aggregated to /24; no customer PII is present.

Attachment stubs: [Redwood_IRP_v2.pdf (PDF), soc2_control_map.csv (CSV), sample_access_logs_20270517.tar.gz (gz)]

A few clarifications:
- The IRP is our current production-facing runbook. Section 3 covers detection/triage (how we identified the anomaly) and Section 5 lists containment and rollback steps we exercised.
- The SOC2/SIG map flags the specific CC and SIG controls that map to our auth/session telemetry. The CSV includes column notes on evidence artifacts.
- For the logs: retention policy limits retention beyond 90 days in raw form; we've created the requested slice and sanitized it as noted. If you need further raw telemetry for internal forensics (with an NDA amendment), we'll escalate to the legal team.

I'll place the files on the secure share and send a link. ETA: secure link in ~45 minutes. If you need a live walkthrough of the IR timeline, I'm available between 4–5pm ET.

—Marissa Cole
Senior Security Engineer, Red Team
Redwood Inference
From: Alicia Reyes <alicia.reyes@graysonbank.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Briefing & request: customer-facing incident — evidence + IR plan

Marissa — thank you, that's exactly what we needed. Quick questions from our forensics lead:
1) Can you confirm whether the session tokens observed in the logs were rotated or invalidated as part of the containment?
2) Is there an associated runbook ticket/incident number in your internal tracker we can reference?

If possible, include the incident ID in the incident summary so our audit trace references the same ticket. We'll review the secure share once you send the link.

Thanks — Alicia
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Alicia Reyes <alicia.reyes@graysonbank.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:32:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Briefing & request: customer-facing incident — evidence + IR plan

Alicia — follow-ups below and link to the secure share.

1) Session handling: during containment we rotated short-lived session keys and forced a graceful token refresh for affected sessions; no long-lived credentials were reissued. Details are summarized in the incident timeline (see IRP Section 5.2).

2) Internal incident tracker: Redwood incident ID R-2027-05-17-17. I've added that ID to the incident summary and the file names on the secure share.

Secure evidence bundle (view-only, audited access): https://drive.redwood.com/secure-share/grayson-2027-incident-evidence

Files on the share (read-only):
- 20270518_R-2027-05-17-17_incident_summary.txt
- Redwood_IRP_v2.pdf
- soc2_control_map.csv
- sample_access_logs_20270517.tar.gz

If you need an executed NDA/ammendment or a signed transfer agreement for expanded telemetry access, loop in your legal team and we'll route to our contracts group. Otherwise, let me know a convenient time for a short walkthrough and we can close the loop for your audit window.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
